Choose a SOM grid size from a grid screen

Source: R/ScreenSOMGrid.R
SelectSOMGrid.Rd

Applies the map-only selection rule to a ScreenSOMGrid() result. Thresholds can be changed and the choice redone without refitting any maps.

  1. Floor: min_nodes_per_variable nodes per clustering variable (default 10), so the mixture step has enough nodes to estimate spread in every dimension.

  2. Ceiling: the smallest of

    • the sparsity ceiling: the largest side before the smoothed one-person share exceeds max_one_person_prop or the smoothed empty share exceeds max_empty_prop;

    • the noise ceiling: the first side whose quantization error is below the expected distance between a person and a retest, sqrt(sum(noise_sd^2)); larger maps only separate people by differences smaller than measurement noise;

    • the cap: max_nodes_per_variable nodes per variable (default 30), or max_nodes if smaller.

  3. Choice: the 5 * sqrt(n) target (Vesanto et al., 2000), moved into the allowed range. If the floor is above the ceiling, the target is kept between the two and a warning is given.

The chosen map is also checked: a warning is given if its topographic error is high compared with the other sides screened (a folded map), or if its trustworthiness is below 0.80.

Usage

SelectSOMGrid(
  x,
  min_nodes_per_variable = 10,
  max_nodes_per_variable = 30,
  max_nodes = NULL,
  max_one_person_prop = 0.1,
  max_empty_prop = 0.05,
  noise_sd = x$settings$jitter_sd,
  select = c("target", "largest_feasible")
)

Arguments

x

A SOMGridScreen object.

min_nodes_per_variable

Floor, in nodes per clustering variable.

max_nodes_per_variable

Cap, in nodes per clustering variable.

max_nodes

Optional absolute cap on the number of nodes.

max_one_person_prop

Largest allowed smoothed share of one-person nodes.

max_empty_prop

Largest allowed smoothed share of empty nodes.

noise_sd

Measurement noise SD in z-score units (one value or one per variable) for the noise ceiling. Defaults to the jitter used in the screen.

select

"target" (default) moves the 5 * sqrt(n) target into the allowed range; "largest_feasible" takes the top of the allowed range.

Value

The screen with updated table pass/fail columns and selection.
